method: Order and injury status come from ESPN's team depth charts. Usage is snap share: the share of the team's offensive, defensive or special-teams snaps a player is projected to play, from nflverse snap counts, a decayed average of this season's games (last season's share for a player with no snaps yet). Passing, rushing and receiving numbers are the NFL model's season projections per game (recent weeks weigh more, last season is the prior, the next opponent's defense adjusts them); touchdowns are his season average, since nothing tested beat it. Pace is offensive plays per game. A player ruled out has no projection. These are projections, not picks. Backtest on 2026 weeks 3 to 8, tuned on 2025, each game projected only from the games before it: Snap share (points), average miss 10.6 vs 11.0 season average and 10.9 last 3 (better than both; by squared error 17.2 vs 17.7, better, 6,340 games); Passing yards, average miss 64.9 vs 67.9 season average and 71.6 last 3 (better than both, 166 games); Rushing yards, average miss 27.4 vs 27.9 season average and 27.7 last 3 (better than both, 257 games); Receptions, average miss 1.76 vs 1.85 season average and 1.92 last 3 (better than both, 739 games); Receiving yards, average miss 24.7 vs 26.0 season average and 26.9 last 3 (better than both, 739 games); Touchdowns, average miss 0.438 vs 0.438 season average and 0.437 last 3 (level with the better one; by squared error 0.636 vs 0.636, level, 1,049 games); Passing touchdowns, average miss 0.965 vs 0.965 season average and 0.981 last 3 (level with the better one; by squared error 1.198 vs 1.198, level, 166 games).
